text:
kevin: Heads up — us-west shared GPU pool went into heavy queueing around 14:32 UTC. Tenant-42 sent a burst of concurrent long-context runs and filled the scheduler slots, we're seeing ~95% slot utilization and p95 queue latency hitting 120s.

maria: :eyes: same tenant that retried a bunch last week? any correlation with retry storms?

kevin: yes, looks similar. retries + big seq lens. A bunch of small requests also piled on so batching got weird.

sam: can we enforce a short-term smoothing window (leaky bucket) per tenant to spread bursts? Even a 30s smoothing should reduce instantaneous slots used.

lydia: we have two constraints: (1) some customers are region-locked (can't route), (2) autoscaler can't add GPUs in us-west — hit soft quota because of maintenance. So routing overflow to other regions isn't always available.

raj: adding to that, dedicated customers shouldn't see drop in throughput; we need weight-preserving fairness so reserved capacity still gets priority.

autoscaler-bot: attempted scale-up +2 gpus in us-west at 14:35 UTC — API quota error: "insufficient-region-capacity".

kevin: ops note — we need graceful degradation: rate-limit best-effort tenants, provide fallback to smaller models for cost-sensitive ones, and smooth admissions.

sam: proposal sketch (very small):
```
# per-tenant leaky bucket (pseudo)
tenant_rate_limit:
  tenant_id: "*"
  bucket_size_tokens: 10      # allow short bursts
  refill_rate_tps: 0.2       # tokens per second => smooth over ~50s
  priority: dynamic         # Reserved tenants bump priority
```
apply at admission gateway before queuing.

maria: can we also couple that with a short-lived circuit-breaker that rejects after X retries to avoid retry amplification?

lydia: yes, we should return structured error with Retry-After and an opt-in for queued receipt so clients can choose async.

raj: we need to be careful with billing implications. If we start rejecting, how do we reflect partial execution vs queued attempts? Ops: show queued vs running tokens in Console.

kevin: agree. Also want a quick dashboard: per-tenant instantaneous slot usage, queue length, retries, avg seq len. I'll add panels.

sam: alternative: smoothing + short windowed weighted fair-queueing (WFQ) where tenant weight decays over time. That preserves fairness across tenants without hard caps. Might be more complex to implement.

lydia: WFQ is nice but we don't currently have per-request weight in the gateway. Might be ~2-3 days to ship. Leaky bucket is quick.

ops-bot: created issue INFRA-2376: "us-west burst smoothing: leaky bucket + retry guidance" assigned to @kevin, due 48h.

kevin: I'll own the quick path: implement leaky-bucket admission + 429 with Retry-After and queued receipt header. We can do WFQ as follow-up if smoothing doesn't reduce p95 queue enough.

maria: small config we should test: bucket_size 8, refill 0.25 tps, allow burst exceptions for reserved tenants with priority tokens. Run on a canary 10% of hosts in us-west.

sam: add a synthetic load test: many tenants with mixed seq_len distributions and retry clients. Compare metrics: peak slots, p95 queue, failed reqs.

raj: please add explicit cost note in the issue — routing overflow to other regions increases egress and inter-region infra costs. For enterprise customers we can waive but need CS approval.

kevin: ack. I'll add cost calc and runbook steps:
- enable smoothing canary in us-west (10%)
- monitor tenant_queue_smoothing panel
- if p95 queue > 60s after 30m, promote to 50%
- if autoscaler still fails and p95 > 90s, enable overflow-route to us-east for only non-region-locked tenants

maria: one more UX detail: include a human-readable reason in 429 body: e.g. "capacity smoothing: try again in 45s or request async job" and a link to docs.

autoscaler-bot: scale-up attempt at 14:38 UTC failed again — quota "maintenance-window".

kevin: timeline: I'll roll the canary in 30m, sam can run the synthetic load before roll. We'll reconvene in this thread with results.

sam: I'll kick off the load script now and post results in ~20m.

lydia: tagging @support to prep customer comms templates if we need to throttle or notify high-volume tenants.

kevin: thanks all — if smoothing reduces instantaneous slot usage by >=30% we can avoid cross-region routing and save $$. 

maria: ack. posting a small note for product: this is not a permanent quota change, just short-term admission control to protect overall health.

raj: also recommend we add a periodic reconciliation job that looks for tenants that consistently hit smoothing and suggest dedicated capacity.

kevin: agreed. Opening follow-ups after canary. :thumbsup:
